title: Distinguish Solar End Customers from Installation Partners
summary: Distinguish Solar End Customers from Installation Partners. Review practical exception decisions, evidence checks, and a copyable Genie job description.
body_markdown:
## Classify the requester’s role in this inquiry


Distinguish a solar end customer from an installation partner using the inquiry’s stated relationship to the project, checked against existing account context. An end customer is enquiring for its own operation; an installation partner is working in a delivery or commercial relationship for customers. A business can play both roles on different projects.


Do not classify solely from a company’s industry. An installer might purchase equipment for its own premises, and a property owner might submit on behalf of a managed portfolio. The useful routing question is what role this requester has in the current inquiry, not which label appears on a directory profile.


Project role unclear: Ask own project or customer project. No speculative final route.; Existing partner relationship: Preserve owner context. No duplicate prospect.; Installer buying for own premises: Classify this inquiry by actual role. Industry label does not decide.

## Ask one clarification that changes the route


When the message is unclear, ask whether the project is for the requester’s own business or for a customer they serve. If they represent another party, ask the relationship needed to route the inquiry, without demanding a full project specification before the first response. Keep the uncertainty visible in HubSpot until answered.


Check whether the account already has an established customer or partner owner. A new inquiry should not erase that relationship. If the project involves a different role from the established one, flag it to the existing owner with the supporting message rather than changing the account’s overall classification without review.


## Build two different follow-up briefs


For an end customer, focus on the stated facility, business need, project decision process, and missing scope. For a partner, focus on the customer project or partnership request, territory, services, and appropriate partner contact. In both cases, distinguish sourced business facts from information still to be confirmed.


Avoid using company size or public revenue estimates to infer budget or readiness to buy. A large company may be exploring a small site, and an installer may be researching a future opportunity. The qualification workflow should improve the first conversation by asking the right questions and routing accurately, rather than prematurely declaring the project qualified for a particular commercial or technical offer.

Apply the organization’s actual policy and source records to the live case; do not treat an illustrative condition as proof that the condition exists.

The underlying commercial inquiry process: match the business, research public context, establish the role, apply owner rules, prepare the brief.


## Illustrative exception and recovery


A solar installer asks about its own office installation. The company’s industry suggests a partner, but the inquiry describes an end-customer project. The brief records that distinction and uses the approved routing rules for the actual request.


This example uses fictional records to show the decision logic. It is not a customer case study or a claim of measured results. In a live case, retain the actual record IDs and evidence behind each statement, and replace all illustrative quantities or timing assumptions with the approved operational inputs.


## What to record before resuming


A sourced HubSpot project brief with the requester’s confirmed role, existing relationship, correct owner, and role-specific follow-up questions.


Preserve the original finding and the evidence that resolves it. Record which person or system supplied the clarification, which proposal it applies to, and the action now permitted. Do not erase the uncertainty from the history: a later reviewer needs to understand why the case paused and why it resumed.


Required systems feed case verification; missing evidence or decisions return to clarification before the workflow proceeds.


## Boundaries that remain in force


-


Check existing account relationships before enrichment or routing.


-


Add sourced business information without treating estimates as verified project facts.


-


Determine end customer versus installation partner from the inquiry and clarify ambiguity.


-


Route to the appropriate owner with a brief and relevant follow-up questions.


## Review the case before restarting


First verify that the new evidence resolves the original blocker rather than a different issue. Then check whether the case, source records, or proposed action changed during the wait. A response attached to the right ticket can still be insufficient if it refers to an earlier proposal or leaves a required quantity, identity, or approval unresolved.


Run the relevant row from the decision table as a review scenario. Confirm that the job stops at the required boundary, asks for the specified information or decision, and resumes from the confirmed state. If a write or message may already have succeeded, inspect its destination before repeating it; if this job only prepares a draft or report, verify that it stays within that output scope.


-


Inquiries routed with an established requester role


-


Ambiguous roles clarified before final routing


-


Company attributes with recorded sources


Track unresolved cases by their actual blocker and owner. A case waiting for clarification needs a different next action from one waiting for a confirmed result. Review the evidence when the state changes, and keep any still-unresolved completion condition visible instead of treating a successful intermediate step as the end of the work.
